maya_cs: Quick check-in on AcmeCorp dedicated pool utilization. Noticed GPU-hours spike last night and steady queue depth at ~18 for the p3-pool. Pulling metrics now, tagging @jordan_ops for ops context. :eyes:
jordan_ops: Saw the alert around 02:10 UTC, CPU on the front-end was fine but queue depth stayed high. I ran a quick drain on non-prod bumpers, helped briefly. Linking perf graph: https://redwood.app/dash/acme/gpu/utilization
liam_eng: thanks for flagging. Do we know if it's sustained inference load or bad batching? Any change in sequence length distribution?
amanda_customer: we had a large batch rerun overnight for embeddings (customer-side). Sorry for the surprise — we queued a backfill. Will throttle future jobs.
maya_cs: good to know, thanks @amanda_customer. For this week: GPU-hours up 42% vs last week (from 720h to 1022h), saturation averaged 79% with a 95th pct queue depth of 21. Cost impact shows ~+11% over committed hours.
jordan_ops: dump of the query I used to get queue depth (CloudWatch -> logs):
```
SELECT avg(queue_depth) AS avg_q, max(queue_depth) AS peak_q, sum(gpu_hours) as total_gpu
FROM ecs_metrics
WHERE cluster = 'acme-dedicated' AND timestamp >= now() - 7d
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day DESC
```
liam_eng: I spot a pattern — most of the increased hours are between 01:00-04:00 UTC. That matches the customer backfill window. If repeated, we should either recommend a scheduled off-peak window or propose burst capacity for those runs.
jordan_ops: Actionable ops items: 1) Apply a soft concurrent-job limit on the acme tenant for non-prod queues (I can apply later today). 2) Add rule to autoscaler to allow short 30-min burst above commit (cost-aware) — needs approval.
maya_cs: I'll propose the burst add-on in the CS playbook and loop in finance for a pricing note. @amanda_customer, would you be open to a 30-min burst option (they would only pay for excess hours)?
amanda_customer: yes that's reasonable. We'll also throttle the backfill to max 4 concurrent workers.
liam_eng: If we enable burst autoscaling, we should pin model variants to 8-bit quantized for backfills to reduce hours. I can prep a one-page recommendation.
jordan_ops: scheduled a short maintenance window to apply limits: 1912502400 (today 18:00 UTC). Deploy-bot: created ticket CS-4532 and scheduled job throttle.
deploy-bot: Ticket CS-4532 created by jordan_ops — "Acme backfill throttle + burst option". ETA: 24h for ops changes, 72h for pricing add-on doc.
maya_cs: Summary/next steps: - Amanda to throttle backfill (customer) - Jordan to apply non-prod concurrent limit and draft burst autoscale rule - Liam to send quantization recommendation - Maya to draft pricing note and renewal flag if surges persist Next sync in 3 days unless escalation needed. :white_check_mark:
